description:
Reggae is a Jamaican music genre that emerged in the late 1960s, developing from earlier styles like ska and rocksteady and quickly becoming the island’s dominant popular music. Defined by a moderate tempo, it has a strong, steady four-beat rhythm and a distinctive emphasis on the offbeat (often called the “skank”), typically played by guitar or keyboards while a deep, prominent bass line anchors the sound. It draws on influences from rhythm and blues, calypso, and other Afro-Caribbean and African-derived traditions. [ 1 ] [ 2 ]

Beyond its musical traits, reggae functions as a cultural and political voice, often associated with Rastafarian spirituality and themes of social justice, resistance, and the struggles of marginalized communities. Through iconic artists such as Bob Marley, the genre moved from Kingston’s ghettos to global stages in the 1970s, becoming an international symbol of Jamaican identity and broader anti-oppression movements. culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Peace, love, social justice, racial pride, black nationalism, anti-colonialism, anti-capitalism, criticism of political systems
